sentences.text: ↵Many services use throttling to control resource consumption, imposing limits on the rate at which applications can access them.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: The rate limiting pattern helps you avoid throttling errors and accurately predict throughput, especially for large-scale repetitive tasks like batch processing.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Performing large numbers of operations against a throttled service can result in increased traffic and reduced efficiency.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Rate limiting reduces traffic and improves throughput by controlling the number of records sent to a service over time.↵Services throttle based on different metrics:↵**Number of operations** (e.g., 20 requests per second)↵**Amount of data** (e.g., 2 GiB per minute)↵**Relative cost of operations** (e.g., 20,000 RUs per second)↵Your rate limiting implementation must control operations sent to the service, optimizing usage without exceeding capacity.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: When your APIs can handle requests faster than throttled services allow, you need to manage ingestion speed.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Simply buffering requests is risky—if your application crashes, you lose buffered data.↵Instead, send records to a durable messaging system that can handle your full ingestion rate.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Use job processors to read records at a controlled rate within the throttled service's limits.↵Durable messaging options include:↵Message queues (e.g., RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ)↵Event streaming platforms (e.g., Apache Kafka)↵Cloud-based queue services↵

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Services often throttle based on comprehensible timespans (per second or per minute), but computers process much faster.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Rather than batching releases once per second, send smaller amounts more frequently to:↵Keep resource consumption (memory, CPU, network) flowing evenly↵Prevent bottlenecks from sudden request bursts↵For example, if a service allows 100 operations per second, release 20 operations every 200 milliseconds:↵

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: When multiple processes share a throttled service, logically partition the service's capacity and use a distributed mutual exclusion system to manage locks on those partitions.↵**Example:**↵If a throttled system allows 500 requests per second:↵Create 20 partitions worth 25 requests per second each↵A process needing 100 requests asks for four partitions↵The system grants two partitions for 10 seconds↵The process rate limits to 50 requests per second, completes in 2 seconds, and releases the lock↵**Implementation approach:**↵Use blob storage to create one small file per logical partition.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Applications obtain exclusive leases on these files for short periods (e.g., 15 seconds).

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: For each lease granted, the application can use that partition's capacity.↵ ↵To reduce latency, allocate a small amount of exclusive capacity for each process.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Processes only seek shared capacity leases when exceeding their reserved capacity.↵Alternative technologies for lease management include Zookeeper, Consul, etcd, and Redis/Redsync.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: :::anote{title="Key Considerations"}↵**Handle throttling errors**: Rate limiting reduces errors but doesn't eliminate them.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Your application must still handle any throttling errors that occur.↵**Multiple workstreams**: If your application has multiple workstreams accessing the same throttled service (e.g., bulk loading and querying), integrate all into your rate limiting strategy or reserve separate capacity pools for each.↵**Multi-application usage**: When multiple applications use the same throttled service, increased throttling errors might indicate contention.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Consider temporarily reducing throughput until usage from other applications decreases.↵:::

sentences.text: Consider an application where users submit records of various types to an API.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Each record type has a unique job processor that performs validation, enrichment, and database insertion.↵All components (API, job processors) are separate processes that scale independently and don't directly communicate.↵ ↵**Workflow:**↵User submits 10,000 records of type A to the API↵API enqueues records in Queue A↵User submits 5,000 records of type B to the API↵API enqueues records in Queue B↵Job Processor A attempts to lease blob 2↵Job Processor B attempts to lease blob 2↵Job Processor A fails; Job Processor B obtains the lease for 15 seconds (100 req/s capacity)↵Job Processor B dequeues and writes 100 records↵After 1 second, both processors attempt additional leases↵Job Processor A obtains blob 6 (100 req/s); Job Processor B obtains blob 3 (now 200 req/s total)↵Processors continue competing for leases and processing records at their granted rates↵As leases expire (after 15 seconds), processors reduce their request rates accordingly

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: **Throttling**: Rate limiting is typically implemented in response to a throttled service.↵**Retry**: When requests result in throttling errors, retry after an appropriate interval.↵**Queue-Based Load Leveling**: Similar but broader than rate limiting.

sourceRef.title: Rate Limiting Pattern: Efficiently Managing Throttled Services

sentences.text: Key differences:↵Rate limiting doesn't necessarily require queues but needs durable messaging↵Rate limiting introduces distributed mutual exclusion on partitions for managing capacity across uncoordinated processes↵Queue-based load leveling applies to any performance mismatch between services; rate limiting specifically addresses throttled services
